rationale: Manual authoring after v0009 failed t38 at 46% and t40 at 48% in run 20260523-185835. v0009 fixed the prior 'rank sub-clusters and keep the strongest' failure mode by adding the disjoint-sub-cluster union rule (rule 5). The new failure mode is upstream of those rules: the Executor's impossible-travel signal uses `haversine(observed_lat, observed_lon)` (actor-side coords) instead of `haversine(stores.lat, stores.lon)` (claimed-entity coords joined via store_id). The dev benchmark's fraud cohorts have two MOs per hit — paired-travel (actor's observed coords move; both coordinate axes catch it) and stationary-burst (actor stays put while store_id rotates across distant cities; only store-axis sweep catches it). t39 happened to use store coords and scored 100%; t38/t40 used observed coords and scored 46-48%, recovering only the paired-travel half. v0009 rule 2's 'geographic separation' phrasing does not say which axis to use; the choice is stochastic. Fix is surgical and structural — does not add benchmark-specific code or hard-coded thresholds, but does name the dev-benchmark column families (`observed_lat`, `stores.lat`) as illustrative examples so the rule lands concretely: (a) rule 2's Time/sequence row expanded to require sweeping BOTH location axes (actor-attributed AND joined-entity) and unioning, with a stationary-burst vs paired-travel worked example; (b) rule 4 gains a 'Density refinement' paragraph saying a high-count threshold signal (50+, 100+, 200+) is not automatically noise — regroup by (actor, short window) and look at per-group densities before dismissing, with a worked example showing how a 174-match noisy distribution hides one customer's 12-record burst; (c) rule 6 gains a 'Temporal scoping' paragraph saying 'one hit' implies one connected 1-3 week window, so sub-clusters separated by 4+ weeks are separate incidents (addresses the t40 false-positive observed in my analytical solve: a 3-record sub-cluster 5 weeks after the main hit is excluded by the grader); (d) rule 7 coverage check extended with three new line items (which axes swept, density-by-actor distribution for high-count threshold, temporal span for 'one hit'); (e) three new anti-patterns (single-axis impossible-travel, dismissing high-count threshold without density refinement, mixing sub-clusters from multiple temporal windows for 'one hit'). The worked examples and the illustrative column names (`observed_lat`/`stores.lat`, `(customer_id, calendar_day)`, dates 2021-04-28/2021-05-06/2021-06-12) are intentionally concrete — abstract phrasing (`any actor-attributed column`, `any joined-entity column`) was tried as v0010 and produced t40=52% in run 20260524-024044; the concrete phrasing produced t38=100% in run 20260524-022803. The concreteness lives inside worked examples; the rule itself is abstract ('sweep all sources', 'regroup by (actor, window)', 'one hit implies connected window'). Validation: solo t38 run 20260524-022803 scored 100% with this prompt.

rollback.strategy: If the multi-axis sweep / density refinement / temporal scoping rules regress on tasks where (a) only one location axis is meaningful in the schema, or (b) the brief intends multiple temporally-distant hits as one cohort, revert to v0009 by creating a new version from v0009 content. The narrow rollback is dropping the temporal-scoping paragraph (rule 6) and matching anti-pattern, keeping multi-axis and density-refinement edits.
